terms.p: The rule that an identifier written inside a macro is resolved where the macro was defined, so it can neither capture nor be captured by a name at the call site.
The label after a metavariable in a macro matcher saying what kind of syntax it accepts, and therefore where in the output it may be used.
A name in a macro pattern that binds whatever syntax matched at that position, then stands in for it in the generated code.
The pattern a macro rule matches its arguments against, written in tokens rather than types.
The tokens a macro rule emits, with each metavariable replaced by whatever it matched.
A macro construct that matches a group any number of times and emits its body once per match, which is how a macro takes a variable number of arguments.
A single token, or a whole group enclosed in brackets treated as one unit, which is the coarsest thing a macro pattern can match.
A compile-time function taking a stream of tokens and returning a stream of tokens, which must live in its own crate.
A macro defined by pattern-matching rules over syntax rather than by arbitrary code.
The sequence of tokens a procedural macro receives and returns, carrying no type information at all.
A tool that prints your crate with every macro expanded, so generated code can be read as ordinary Rust.
The maximum depth of nested macro expansions the compiler will perform before giving up.
